lines.text: Stretch a right triangle over a grid of dots. How many dots end up inside?
lines.caption: Stretch a right triangle over a grid of dots. How many dots end up inside?

lines.text: We need EXACTLY ten inside, and the slanted side is sneaky.
lines.caption: We need EXACTLY ten inside, and the slanted side is sneaky.

lines.text: Hello, I'm Vantee. Let's count some dots!
lines.caption: Hello, I'm Vantee. Let's count some dots!

lines.text: Here's the question. A right triangle has corners at zero zero, p zero, and zero q.
lines.caption: Here's the question. A right triangle has corners at zero zero, p zero, and zero q.

lines.text: Here p and q are positive whole numbers.
lines.caption: Here p and q are positive whole numbers.

lines.text: Exactly ten points with whole-number coordinates lie strictly inside it.
lines.caption: Exactly ten points with whole-number coordinates lie strictly inside it.

lines.text: How many ordered pairs, p and then q, are possible?
lines.caption: How many ordered pairs, p and then q, are possible?

lines.text: The legs lie along the axes: p across and q up.
lines.caption: The legs lie along the axes: p across and q up.

lines.text: Strictly inside means dots on the edges do NOT count.
lines.caption: Strictly inside means dots on the edges do NOT count.

lines.text: Ordered pairs means two and twenty-one is different from twenty-one and two.
lines.caption: Ordered pairs means two and twenty-one is different from twenty-one and two.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

scenes.chapter: Solution 1: cut a rectangle in half

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's add a twin triangle to make a rectangle. First, a six by four one.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's add a twin triangle to make a rectangle. First, a six by four one.

lines.text: Inside are five across and three up: fifteen dots.
lines.caption: Inside are five across and three up: fifteen dots.

lines.text: The slanted side cuts the rectangle into two triangles. One dot sits right ON it.
lines.caption: The slanted side cuts the rectangle into two triangles. One dot sits right ON it.

lines.text: Turn it half a turn and the triangles swap, so the other fourteen dots split evenly: seven each.
lines.caption: Turn it half a turn and the triangles swap, so the other fourteen dots split evenly: seven each.

lines.text: Now any p by q rectangle. It holds p minus one, times q minus one, dots inside.
lines.caption: Now any p by q rectangle. It holds p minus one, times q minus one, dots inside.

lines.text: Call g the greatest common factor of p and q.
lines.caption: Call g the greatest common factor of p and q.

lines.text: The slant splits into g equal hops, so g minus one dots sit strictly between its ends.
lines.caption: The slant splits into g equal hops, so g minus one dots sit strictly between its ends.

lines.text: Take those away, then split in half. Ten in each half means the rest is twenty.
lines.caption: Take those away, then split in half. Ten in each half means the rest is twenty.

lines.text: Add g minus one to both sides: p minus one, times q minus one, equals nineteen plus g.
lines.caption: Add g minus one to both sides: p minus one, times q minus one, equals nineteen plus g.

lines.text: Let's call p the shorter leg for now. We'll flip the pairs at the end.
lines.caption: Let's call p the shorter leg for now. We'll flip the pairs at the end.

lines.text: If both legs were seven or more, the triangle would cover a seven by seven triangle.
lines.caption: If both legs were seven or more, the triangle would cover a seven by seven triangle.

lines.text: That one has thirty-six minus six, thirty dots, and half is fifteen. Too many!
lines.caption: That one has thirty-six minus six, thirty dots, and half is fifteen. Too many!

lines.text: So the short leg p is at most six. And p equals one leaves no room inside.
lines.caption: So the short leg p is at most six. And p equals one leaves no room inside.

lines.text: Now try p from two to six. Remember, g must be a factor of p.
lines.caption: Now try p from two to six. Remember, g must be a factor of p.

lines.text: p equals two: g is one or two, so q is twenty-one or twenty-two. Both check out!
lines.caption: p equals two: g is one or two, so q is twenty-one or twenty-two. Both check out!

lines.text: p equals three: two times q minus one is twenty or twenty-two. So q is eleven or twelve.
lines.caption: p equals three: two times q minus one is twenty or twenty-two. So q is eleven or twelve.

lines.text: p equals four: only twenty-one splits into threes, so q is eight. But four and eight share four, not two!
lines.caption: p equals four: only twenty-one splits into threes, so q is eight. But four and eight share four, not two!

lines.text: p equals five: q is six or seven. Five and six works, but five and seven don't share a five!
lines.caption: p equals five: q is six or seven. Five and six works, but five and seven don't share a five!

lines.text: p equals six: only twenty and twenty-five split into fives.
lines.caption: p equals six: only twenty and twenty-five split into fives.

lines.text: Twenty gives q equals five, already counted. Twenty-five gives q equals six!
lines.caption: Twenty gives q equals five, already counted. Twenty-five gives q equals six!

lines.text: Five of our six pairs have different legs, so flipping gives ten ordered pairs.
lines.caption: Five of our six pairs have different legs, so flipping gives ten ordered pairs.

lines.text: Six and six flips into itself, so it counts once. Ten plus one is eleven. That's Choice D!
lines.caption: Six and six flips into itself, so it counts once. Ten plus one is eleven. That's Choice D!

lines.text: Pick's theorem gives a faster road. Area equals the dots inside, plus half the edge dots, minus one.
lines.caption: Pick's theorem gives a faster road. Area equals the dots inside, plus half the edge dots, minus one.

lines.text: Walk the edge: p steps along the bottom, g hops up the slant, q steps down. That's p plus q plus g.
lines.caption: Walk the edge: p steps along the bottom, g hops up the slant, q steps down. That's p plus q plus g.

lines.text: The area is p times q over two. That equals ten, plus half of p plus q plus the letter g, minus one.
lines.caption: The area is p times q over two. That equals ten, plus half of p plus q plus the letter g, minus one.

lines.text: Double it and tidy up: p minus one, times q minus one, equals nineteen plus g. Same equation!
lines.caption: Double it and tidy up: p minus one, times q minus one, equals nineteen plus g. Same equation!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? It's quick if you know the theorem. The rectangle works if you don't.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? It's quick if you know the theorem. The rectangle works if you don't.

lines.text: Choice E, twelve, is what you'd get if you flipped all six pairs. But six and six flipped is itself!
lines.caption: Choice E, twelve, is what you'd get if you flipped all six pairs. But six and six flipped is itself!

lines.text: Choice C, ten, is what you'd get if you missed six and six. Its slanted side hides five dots!
lines.caption: Choice C, ten, is what you'd get if you missed six and six. Its slanted side hides five dots!

lines.text: Choice B, six, is what you'd get if you never flipped, or if you forgot the dots on the slant.
lines.caption: Choice B, six, is what you'd get if you never flipped, or if you forgot the dots on the slant.

lines.text: Choice A, five, is what you'd get if you kept only p smaller than q, and never flipped.
lines.caption: Choice A, five, is what you'd get if you kept only p smaller than q, and never flipped.

lines.text: Your turn! Same triangle, but now exactly six dots lie inside. How many ordered pairs this time?
lines.caption: Your turn! Same triangle, but now exactly six dots lie inside. How many ordered pairs this time?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Now the rest must be twelve, so p minus one, times q minus one, equals eleven plus g.
lines.caption: Now the rest must be twelve, so p minus one, times q minus one, equals eleven plus g.

lines.text: A six by six triangle has ten dots inside. Too many, so the short leg is at most five.
lines.caption: A six by six triangle has ten dots inside. Too many, so the short leg is at most five.

lines.text: p equals two gives q equals thirteen or fourteen.
lines.caption: p equals two gives q equals thirteen or fourteen.

lines.text: p equals three gives q equals seven. Eight fails, because three and eight don't share a three.
lines.caption: p equals three gives q equals seven. Eight fails, because three and eight don't share a three.

lines.text: p equals four gives q equals five. Six fails, because four and six share two, not four.
lines.caption: p equals four gives q equals five. Six fails, because four and six share two, not four.

lines.text: p equals five: q is four, already counted, or five. And five and five do share a five.
lines.caption: p equals five: q is four, already counted, or five. And five and five do share a five.

lines.text: Four pairs flip into eight. Add five, five: nine ordered pairs! Fantastic work if you got it.
lines.caption: Four pairs flip into eight. Add five, five: nine ordered pairs! Fantastic work if you got it.

lines.text: Here's the big idea: count the rectangle's dots, take away the ones on the slant, and split in half.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea: count the rectangle's dots, take away the ones on the slant, and split in half.

lines.text: Then keep the short leg small, and check each case.
lines.caption: Then keep the short leg small, and check each case.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
